key_insight: The paper introduces trapdoored Clifford distributions that look random to outsiders but can be sampled and implemented much faster when a secret trapdoor is available.
engineering_relevance: This could make randomized benchmarking, classical shadows, quantum authentication, and related Clifford-based protocols far more practical for larger quantum systems.
method: Constructs trapdoored Clifford operators under a learning-parity-with-noise-style assumption.
Provides fast tableau updates for classical simulation and polylog-depth implementation options.
Builds trapdoored finite-field matrices with efficient forward and inverse multiplication, enabling Clifford and matrix applications.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports cryptographic indistinguishability guarantees, near-linear sampling/implementation, polylog-depth variants, and hardness reductions tied to matrix multiplication and Clifford synthesis.
watch_item: The speedups and security properties depend on cryptographic assumptions, so practical deployment may be limited if those assumptions weaken or if trapdoor generation becomes costly.
